Q: Tkinter Canvas create_image() method not working A:

There is well known problem with bug in PhotoImage which removes image when it is assigned to local variable. It needs to assign image to global variable or use self. to assign to class/instance variable.

You have self.images.update({image: id}) which should resolve it
but your code has little different problem with this bug.
It needs also to assign class to global variable:

chess = ChessBoard(root)

And this works for me.

It needs both chess = ... and self.images.update(...) to work correctly.

I tested it with only one image because it doesn't need to download and rename files.

Full code used for tests (with few other changes)

            x = col * 100 + 50

root.geometry("800x800")

Q: What is a Jenkins Workspace directory? A:

The file should be in 

 c:\jenkins\workspace\mxnet\mxnet\src\operator\elemwise_op_common.h

The \../ being for getting one folder up.

The workspace is where Jenkins checks out the sources, and execute its job.
It differs from a build.
See more at "Building a software project".

Q: How to cull a pair based of relative distance between the centre of two objects? A:

You don't need to calculate the actual distance with abs() and sqrt() just to determine whether two circles overlap.

Compare the squared distance between their centers with the squared sum of their radii:

dx = other.position.x - self.position.x
dy = other.position.y - self.position.y

distance_squared = dx * dx + dy * dy
radius_sum = self.radius + other.radius

if 0 < distance_squared <= radius_sum * radius_sum:
    # The objects are close enough to collide
    ...

This avoids calculating the square root required to obtain the actual distance.

If vectogebra.vector supports vector subtraction and multiplication, you can also use the vector itself:

delta = other.position - self.position
distance_squared = delta.x * delta.x + delta.y * delta.y

radius_sum = self.radius + other.radius

if 0 < distance_squared <= radius_sum * radius_sum:
    # collision candidate
    ...

There is also a separate issue in your code: you calculate the unit normal before checking whether the objects are close enough:

self.unit_body_normal = (other.position - self.position) / abs(self.position - other.position)

That calculation should only happen after the distance test succeeds. Otherwise you're doing vector operations for pairs that you are going to discard anyway.

For a physics engine with many objects, the bigger optimization is usually to avoid generating all possible pairs in the first place. A broad-phase method such as a uniform spatial grid, spatial hash, quadtree, or sweep-and-prune can reduce the number of pairs that reach this collision test.

So, for a simple optimization, use squared distances. For a large simulation, use a broad-phase collision algorithm as well.
